messages:
Morgan: FYI we started seeing a big latency spike after today's runtime release — +30% median on gen tests. Rolling CI job failed on perf guard.
Brian: I see a compile storm in the logs — thousands of kernel compiles for the same model/seq range within minutes.
Chang: dug in a bit. The selector heuristic changed in commit abc123 — it now prefers the 'wide-kernel' path for mid-length sequences. That shouldn't normally trigger compiles that many times.
Callie: do we have example logs? paste from prod:
```
2026-03-18T14:12:33Z INFO compiling kernel model=redwood-v2 seq=256 batch=4 opt=wide-kernel
timestamp=161... compiled_kernel_id=0x7f8
2026-03-18T14:12:34Z INFO compiling kernel model=redwood-v2 seq=256 batch=4 opt=wide-kernel
```
Brian: same compile repeated with small TTL gaps. Looks like KV cache churn — compiled kernels not being reused.
Prashant: interesting — the cache key generation changed in the heuristic PR. It now includes batch as the last component but we read keys as batch-first in the cache lookup. So keys don't match and we miss hits.
Morgan: oh wow. So selector picks the same kernel repeatedly, but cache misses force recompile each time -> compile storm.
Callie: here's the snippet I pulled from the commit (simplified):
```
# new (buggy)
key = f"{model}:{seq}:{shard}:{batch}"
# lookup uses old ordering: model:batch:seq:shard
```
Chang: Confirmed on a repro run locally — flip the ordering back and cache hit rate goes from ~2% to ~95%.
Prashant: CI perf guard flagged the regression at job r-tests/serve-perf. Bisect points to abc123 which was merged in the runtime heuristics PR.
Brian: I'm going to trigger an emergency rollback of that merge from the cluster (rolling revert flag). Callie can you prepare a canary after revert?
Callie: on it. Patching feature-flag to force-old-selector and starting canary infra now. Will post link to canary dashboard.
deploy-bot: revert of merge abc123 queued by Brian — change-id: revert-abc123 — started at 2026-03-18T14:22:00Z
Morgan: good. After canary stabilizes we should add a unit/integration test that asserts stable cache key shape across selector codepaths.
Chang: also adding a small fuzz test that validates cache lookup vs generation ordering across variants.
Prashant: heads-up for postmortem: note the root cause = cache-key ordering mismatch + heuristic change causing selector to hit the path more often. Action items: revert (done), add tests, add CI perf regression test simulating repeated small sequences, and add a liveness alarm for compile rate spikes.
Brian: will follow up with a PR to fix the key generation and add the test. Assigning to me + Chang.
Callie: canary dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/canary/2012504321 — latency back to baseline after rolling revert :thumbsup:
Morgan: thanks everyone. We'll schedule a short retro tomorrow.
